newsitem.title: USA: Federal Express lifts freight fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Federal Express lifts freight fuel surcharge.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said Tuesday it discontinued its fuel surcharge effective June 1 on FedEx International Express Freight and FedEx Airport-to-Airport services originating in the U.S., Canada and Asia.
For U.S. domestic service shipments and FedEx International Priority shipments originating in the U.S., the surcharge is scheduled to be lifted on August 1, the company said.

Federal Express said it had initiated the surcharge on the two international freight services in December 1996 after absorbing increasing jet fuel costs for months. The fuel surcharge on the remaining services was delayed until February 1997 to allow Federal Express customers to get through their peak shipping season, the company said.
On April 15, Federal Express said it removed the fuel surcharge on FedEx International Express Freight and FedEx Airport-to-Airport services originating in Europe and Latin America.
